question: What is the best flooring for a vacation rental in Florida?
title: Best Flooring for a Florida Vacation Rental
h1: What's the Best Flooring for a Florida Vacation Rental?
description: Waterproof rigid-core LVP with a 20-mil wear layer or porcelain tile hold up best for Florida rentals in 2026. Skip carpet and solid hardwood.
capsule: Waterproof rigid-core LVP with at least a 20-mil wear layer, or porcelain tile, are the standard picks for Florida vacation rentals. Both shed sand and moisture and outlast the standard 12-mil residential wear layer under guest turnover. Skip carpet, which traps sand and moisture, and solid hardwood, which is harder to protect between bookings.

sections.h2: Why Carpet and Solid Hardwood Are the Wrong Call Here
sections.html:
Beach-area rental guidance is consistent on this point: avoid carpet, which traps sand and holds moisture between cleanings, and avoid solid hardwood, which is harder to protect from the sand, wet swimsuits, and rolling luggage that come with constant guest turnover. Waterproof rigid-core LVP or porcelain tile handle both problems better.

This holds along the barrier islands especially, Siesta Key, Longboat Key, Anna Maria Island, where guests track sand in from the beach multiple times a day during peak season. A floor that can't shed that sand without scratching or staining turns into a maintenance problem within a single busy month, not a slow decline over years. We don't recommend engineered or solid hardwood for any rental within walking distance of the beach, regardless of how well-sealed the finish is, since repeated moisture exposure eventually finds a seam.

sections.h2: LVP or Tile: What Actually Holds Up to Guest Turnover
sections.html:
Wear layer thickness is the number that matters most for LVP in a rental. Standard residential product uses a 12-mil wear layer, 0.012 inch, while 20-mil, 0.020 inch, is the usual commercial-grade minimum and the level typically recommended for large dogs, kids, and rental properties. Porcelain tile skips the wear-layer question entirely since it's a hard, non-organic surface that doesn't scratch the same way.

Grout is the other variable owners underestimate. Even with porcelain tile's durability, unsealed or poorly maintained grout lines can hold onto sand, sunscreen residue, and stains from spilled drinks between cleanings. A quality grout sealer applied at installation, and reapplied periodically, keeps that maintenance manageable across dozens of guest turnovers a year. That's a conversation worth having with your cleaning crew from day one, not something to figure out after the first complaint about dingy grout lines.

Our typical 2026 local ranges run $1.75-$3.25 per square foot for standard 12-mil LVP, $2.75-$5.50 for mid-range 20-mil SPC, and $6-$10 for 12-18 inch porcelain tile. This Old House's national figures land higher and broader, $5-$17 per square foot for standard plank and $6-$20 for LVP once material and labor are combined, which shows how much local pricing can undercut a national blended average.

Labor tends to make up a larger share of the LVP number than the material itself, especially on a job that also involves removing an old floor first. Tile's installed range reflects more labor-intensive setting and grouting work, which is part of why it costs more per square foot even though the raw material isn't always pricier than premium LVP.

sections.h2: What We Check Before Recommending a Rental Floor
sections.html:
Every quote starts with a slab moisture reading, since a rental that turns over every few days doesn't give you room for a floor failure later. We write a line-itemized quote so you can see material, labor, and any waterproof underlayment as separate costs, and back the work with our two-year written workmanship warranty. If beach exposure is part of the picture, our waterproof flooring page covers the specifics.

Properties on Siesta Key and other barrier-island addresses also tend to see more moisture exposure from salt air, which is one more reason we don't skip the slab moisture reading on a beach rental even when the floor looks fine on the surface. Ask about grout sealing and waterproof underlayment options in the same visit, so the full picture, material, labor, and long-term upkeep, is on one written quote. That's the version of the number that actually helps you budget across a full season of bookings, not just the install day.

faqs.q: Is 12-mil LVP ever okay for a vacation rental?
faqs.a: It can work for a low-traffic secondary space, but a 20-mil wear layer is the usual recommendation once you're dealing with regular guest turnover, sand, and rolling luggage.

faqs.q: Does tile cost more than LVP for a rental?
faqs.a: Generally yes per our local ranges, though tile's grout lines need more upkeep between bookings than a click LVP floor does; both are reasonable choices depending on your cleaning turnaround.

faqs.q: What about a property close to the beach or bay?
faqs.a: Waterproof rigid-core LVP or porcelain tile are the two materials that handle occasional sand and moisture exposure without the risk carpet or solid hardwood carry.
